Vendor-only ABI: conv_tiles.py opens /dev/dri/card1 and submits through DRM_IOCTL_RKNPU_MEM_CREATE/MEM_MAP/MEM_SYNC/ACTION/SUBMIT with struct rknpu_submit and RKNPU_JOB_PC. It has no rocket_runtime or drm_rocket_task path. Re-hosting its register builder would require a new BO/submission adapter and fresh verification; producing a READY bundle would imply an unverified Rocket ABI. No registers were invented.

No Rocket-capable FP16 builder emits and validates CNA_PAD_CON0. conv_new_clean.py comments the pad register out (lines 547-550) and computes valid-only geometry. conv_mesa_fp16.py does emit CNA_PAD_CON0, but its register path is the Mesa uint8 zero-point semantics (for example BS_OW_OP uses 0x80 - weights_zero_point and OUT_CVT/EW scales are quantized), so using it would change the numerical contract. A true pad-register FP16 case is therefore blocked pending source evidence and tests. The READY padded case uses an explicit zero frame instead.

Split-K reduction requires accumulation of partial products across tiles. Neither inspected Rocket path provides an accumulator or a second reduction pass: conv_0522._execute_conv_tiles clears the output BO before every tile and _tile_to_desc leaves all tile offsets at zero; conv_new_clean has no K-split for spatial conv. Only split-OC is encoded as READY. Adding split-K would require a new accumulation contract, not just more tasks.

cases.blocked_reason: No source path encodes a convolution stride.  The FP16 shape parser accepts an sN field (expt/conv_simple.py:228-238), but _conv_params ignores it (lines 297-311) and make_regs always writes CNA_CONV_CON3 = (1<<3)|1 = 0x9, i.e. stride 1 (expt/conv_simple.py:408).  kernel_6_18/simple_conv.py hardcodes the same value at line 557.  Emitting a stride-2 case would require a new CNA_CONV_CON3 encoding that these sources do not provide.

No SAME-padding path exists in the named sources.  The FP16 make_regs() never writes CNA_PAD_CON0 or CNA_PAD_CON1 (expt/conv_simple.py:383-440) and _conv_params computes out_h/out_w = in_h/in_w - k + 1, i.e. valid-only (expt/conv_simple.py:301).  The INT8 builder writes CNA_PAD_CON0 = 0 (kernel_6_18/simple_conv.py:575), sets CNA_PAD_CON1 only to a zero-point fill value (line 584), and also computes valid-only output geometry (lines 81-82).  A SAME case would require new pad-register evidence and an output-with-halo contract that the sources do not provide.

This C8 shape cannot be packed safely with the FP16 builder.  For in_c=8, _conv_align_c returns 16 (expt/conv_simple.py:283-286), but _conv_input_pack_c2 returns 8 (lines 289-294).  pack_input() then writes c1*c2 = 8 channels per pixel (lines 364-374), while make_regs sets CNA_DATA_SIZE1 = ((in_c-1)<<16) | data_in_channel_aligned = 0x00070010, i.e. a 16-channel aligned field (lines 393,410).  The source's own known-supported table has no C8 entry (lines 207-217), and its validated small-channel path is the <=4-channel NHWC case (C3/C4, where use_nhwc is true and the CVT fields carry the real channel count).  There is no source-supported padding contract that fills the missing 8 channels for C8 (the same gap affects 5 <= in_c <= 8).  The READY small cases therefore use C4, and the larger cases use C16/C32 where the packed channel count equals the aligned count.

The grouped path cannot be expressed safely from these sources.  The FP16 make_regs() has no group-count register and its known-supported table has no grouped entry (expt/conv_simple.py:207-217,383-440).  The only grouped implementation is kernel_6_18/simple_conv.py::run_conv2d_grouped (lines 729-759), which slices input/weight/bias and calls run_conv2d_shape once per group; each call overwrites the shared BOs in write_buffers (lines 675-691) and does its own npu_submit (lines 871-872).  A single bundle would therefore need per-group BOs plus a multi-task PC chain, and the chain's PC_BASE_ADDRESS would have to be regcmd_addr + task_offset.  The bundle patch schema can only bind named buffer addresses, not the regcmd self-address, so the chain cannot be encoded without leaving an unpatched address.

The source's addition-input knobs are not a usable ABI.  use_shape() reads addition_input/add_tensor (kernel_6_18/simple_conv.py:83-84), but build_conv_regs() uses them only to change CNA_PAD_CON1 and the single-channel CVT scale (lines 523-531); add_tensor is never written to an address register.  write_buffers() allocates and packs only input/weight/bias/output (lines 675-691), and npu_submit() submits no addition tensor BO (lines 298-305).  A residual case would require a vendor-only addition-input stream and a second feature buffer, which these sources do not construct.

The source proves DIV/FLOOR/CEIL use floating-point semantics and are not integer operations (OPERATIONS[...]['integer_supported'] = False). There is no trustworthy integer oracle; bundling them as integer EW would mislabel the result. FLOOR and CEIL share this blocker.

The only multi-input sum in either source is FP16, with FP32 BRDMA/NRDMA operands. This family is integer-only (ew-int); an FP16/FP32 mixed case needs its own oracle and belongs in an ew-fp16 family. It is not an INT8/INT16/INT32 case and was deliberately not materialized here.
ReLU-X and PReLU are emitted only in the FP16 BS/BN auxiliary stages. No integer ReLU path exists in either source, and ReLU6 and batchnorm are never emitted at all. Not an integer elementwise case.

Source expt/pooling.py docstring lines 17-18 and the case flag expect_unsupported=True (lines 937-962) report that this PROC_PRECISION configuration submits successfully (submit_ret==0) but writes all zero, while the expected maximum is nonzero. That disproves the format on this PPU path; there is no valid output to compare. The exact probe stream is retained, but it must not be scored as a READY numerical case.

format_observations.message: The current CAPTURE_FORMAT.md contains a 'Rocket job boundary' paragraph stating that multiple sequential RK submissions must not share one tasks array. This audit rerun was scoped to the fetch-parity padding rule; the multi-task cases below were not reclassified under that newer paragraph and need separate review.
